I have only had one pet become very ill before the end of their expected life, and fortunately I was insured.

My 4yr old dog was urinating a lot, so I took her to the vet thinking it was a UTI, in the waiting room I found a tiny less than pea sized lump by her ear. I mentioned it to the vet thinking it was a sign of infection, a swollen gland like humans get with infections. The vet did a full check of her and said "she seems to have a case of the lumpy bumpys". In my response; I thought that sounds OK so asked him what the treatment was. That is when he explained how bad it could be.

That was a friday and it was a bank holiday weekend, the biopsy was booked in for Tuesday, in those 3 days the lumps grew to the size of baseballs. The biopsy results came in on the Friday: Acute Lymphatic cancer, she was peeing so much because she was dying. I had a choice, put her down there and then or try for chemo. She was happy, seemed to have no pain and I had the insurance.

The nearest vet who could do it was 200 miles away, so we booked in with him for the following Monday ( I got a severe telling off from my boss)

By the time we got to the Chemo vet she was very ill...only 10 days after finding that tiny lump , well, I thought it was over. The chemo vet did a lot of tests and kept her in. I said goodbye that night, or so I thought. Went home and took ANOTHER day off

So another 400 mile round trip and 24 hrs later, she was a different dog.

So end result a happy dog, one really really pissed off boss, 800 miles on the car. We had to go back every Tuesday...so we did, for 8 weeks (so that's a lot of miles and a lot of lost sleep, I was getting home after midnight)

In the end, the chemo failed and I took her for a big long walk, she ran, she swam, she played with sticks: and then I walked in to my home vets with a happy muddy, tail wagging friend who the night before had vomited up the water she had drunk, the lumps were too big

End result over £7000 in vets fees ( paid by for insurance),over 4000 miles of travel, a boss who sacked me, £68 for the euthanasia.

The real cost was losing a dog and a friend I loved., and still miss.

What was my pets life worth?

It was worth every effort and care I could make, it was worth spending hours and hours trying to help her, and it was worth my pain in killing her when she was in pain, because it was the least I could do for her in the end.

My dogs life was worth my tears
